close_reason: Closed in ee6b41e via doc-contract tightening (Path B from the bead description). The trait method's rustdoc now pins 4 output-shape requirements: fixed length, >= 128 bits CSPRNG entropy, ASCII-safe encoding (no /, +, =, whitespace, no non-ASCII), and sufficient lifespan. The reference MemoryBackend impl already satisfies all four (16 bytes getrandom + lowercase hex = 32 chars) so no impl change was needed; the contract makes the existing invariants explicit. Items 3 (sync) and 4 (infallible) from the bead description were filed as follow-up bd:JMAP-x2gd.36.1 (human-labeled, recommended to defer until .50 / .46.1 / .43 sync-vs-async + per-account-args family is taken as a single workspace-architectural pass). The full async-fallible rewrite (Path A from the bead body) was deferred because the parent epic's own confidence note hedged on that direction ('a senior reviewer might prefer documenting the length contract and keeping sync').
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:284-310

  fn generate_invite_code(&self) -> String;

The trait doc correctly mandates CSPRNG entropy (per
workspace AGENTS.md 'secret-minting methods require CSPRNG'). It
also names the constant-time-compare contract for consumers of
the code (handle_space_join). What it does NOT pin:

1. LENGTH. The handle_space_join site (space.rs:1305-1310)
   comments: 'canonical generator emits fixed-length (32 hex
   chars) codes, so the length is effectively public — only the
   content needs constant-time protection.' This invariant is
   load-bearing for the constant-time argument: ConstantTimeEq's
   ct_eq returns Choice(0) cheaply on length mismatch, so a
   backend that emits variable-length codes leaks a length
   oracle through the timing channel that ct_eq cannot mask. A
   consumer reading the trait doc has no way to know they must
   produce fixed-length output.

2. CHARSET / ENCODING. The string could be base64, base64url,
   hex, base58, raw bytes interpreted as UTF-8, etc. The kit
   does not constrain what shape the code takes. If a backend
   produces base64 codes with embedded slashes, downstream URL-
   encoded redemption flows break. If it produces non-ASCII, the
   helpers::iso8601_before slicing pattern panics on non-ASCII
   input (JMAP-x2gd.20 already flagged the helper's brittleness).

3. FALLIBILITY. The signature is -> String, not -> io::Result<String>
   or Result<String, E>. A backend that wants to call out to an HSM,
   KMS, or any other potentially-failing entropy source has no way
   to surface failure — the trait forces panicking on entropy
   starvation (getrandom errors are rare but real on container
   startup and on hardened sandboxes).

4. SYNC, not async. Backends backed by a remote KMS cannot await.
   They have to .block_on() inside a sync trait method — never
   acceptable in a tokio context.

Fix shape:

  /// Must be at least 32 bytes of CSPRNG entropy, encoded as
  /// ASCII-safe (RECOMMENDED: lowercase hex, 64 chars output).
  /// Length MUST be deterministic across calls.
  fn generate_invite_code(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<String, Self::Error>> + Send;

Plus a documented "if you can't pin length, the constant-time
compare in handle_space_join is broken for you and you must
either pin or use a different redemption path" note.

The kit-versus-consumer split lets the kit commit to its constant-
time invariant only when the backend honors the length / encoding
contract. Today the kit assumes the contract without naming it.
title: API contract: generate_invite_code has no length / charset / fallibility contract
